title: The Sahara
about: its area, the countries it covers and its hottest temperatures. Include several specific numbers, dates or names where the topic has them, some exact and some rounded or hedged (about, nearly, more than, up to).
passages: The Sahara is the largest hot desert on Earth. It covers about 9.2 million square kilometers, or roughly 3.6 million square miles, which makes it nearly as big as the United States. It stretches across northern Africa from the Atlantic Ocean in the west to the Red Sea in the east. It reaches into 11 countries and TERRITORIES, including Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Niger, Chad and Sudan. Many people picture endless sand dunes, but dunes cover only a small part of it. Much of the Sahara is bare rock, gravel plains and high, windy plateaus.

Summer days in the Sahara are SCORCHING. Air temperatures often climb above 40 degrees Celsius, and in July 2018 a weather station in Ouargla, Algeria, recorded 51.3 degrees. That is one of the highest reliable readings ever taken in Africa. The sand itself can get even hotter, up to roughly 70 degrees. For more than a thousand years, NOMADIC peoples such as the Tuareg have crossed this land with camel CARAVANS. They travel between OASES, green spots where water comes up from deep underground. Many Tuareg men wear a long indigo veil to protect their faces from wind, dust and sun.
